summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of prior strokes, COPD, CAD s/p CABG, and esophagitis was admitted for acute vertigo and chest pain. Initial concern for stroke was raised due to his neurological history, but MRI/MRA showed no acute infarct, with findings consistent with chronic small vessel disease. Vertigo improved with supportive care and discontinuation of trazodone, which may have contributed to dizziness. Chest pain was attributed to chronic esophagitis and resolved with continuation of PPI and sucralfate. A 3 mm right upper lobe pulmonary nodule was incidentally found on CTA, prompting recommendation for follow-up imaging in one year. The patient was discharged home with services, advised to follow up with primary care and neurology, and medication changes were discussed, including the correction of an intended lisinopril prescription due to allergy.
